solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Issue featuring oddly neglected Welsh headland

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word Welsh are ignored, keeping only its second and fourth

parts.note: a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A publication or edition containing something about a promontory on the Welsh coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to flow or come out, which is what something does when it gets free; as nouns, an outflow or leak is an issue.

clue.text: Muse over weed coming from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming from the south means the letters are read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a tare is a weed, such as vetch, that grows among corn

explanation.surface: Someone ponders a patch of weeds creeping up from the southern end of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder, but it is the noun: one of the nine Greek Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the patron of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Completed after prisoner gets pardon

indicators.note: after places the word for completed behind the word for prisoner

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
done means completed or finished

explanation.surface: Once a convict has served the full sentence, a pardon is granted.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or forgive an offence, a close synonym of pardon as a verb.

clue.text: Miscellany from Prospect's first issue looking into development of riot

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word Prospect
looking into puts the word for issue inside the scrambled letters, as if peering in
development means the letters of riot are worked into a new form

parts.note: to pour is to issue or flow out in quantity

explanation.surface: A magazine's first edition investigates how a riot developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a magazine edition, matching 'Prospect', but here it is the verb meaning flow out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-pourri is a mixed collection of things, so it serves as a synonym for a miscellany or medley.

clue.text: Arranged for expert on Poland to meet head of department

indicators.note: in an across clue, one word on another follows it, so the expert comes after Poland

parts.note: PL is the international abbreviation for Poland
an ace is an expert, a top performer

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the word department

explanation.surface: A specialist in Polish affairs has been set up to meet a departmental chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed means put in position or set out, the same sense as arranged in a past tense.

clue.text: The worst parts include Dominica's capital city

indicators.note: include puts the chosen letter inside the word for dregs

parts.note: lees are the dregs, the sediment and worst part of wine

indicators.note: capital means the initial, upper-case letter of Dominica

explanation.surface: The worst districts take in the capital of the Caribbean island Dominica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts you towards Roseau, Dominica's capital city; it only takes its first letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, England, so 'city' is a plain example definition.

clue.text: Reckon on soldiers coming around the opposite way

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another follows it below, so the soldiers come after

parts.note: to count is to reckon or calculate

indicators.note: coming around turns the soldiers' abbreviation back to front

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Counting on troops to circle back the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Counter used as an adverb means in the contrary direction, as in running counter to the trend.

clue.text: Utterly different from despair at being abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests the letters are let loose with no order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling quite unlike someone in despair at being deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate things are so unlike that they cannot be compared, which is being entirely different.

clue.text: Worry about equipment for catching small birds

indicators.note: about turns the word for worry around

parts.note: to nag is to worry or pester someone
a net is gear for catching fish or butterflies
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher frets over whether there is the right gear to trap little birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Gannets are large diving seabirds, so the plural noun 'birds' covers them as examples.

clue.text: Ask for English queen inside to be at ease

indicators.note: inside puts the two short pieces within the word for relaxing

parts.note: to rest is to be at ease, relaxing

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an English queen to be made comfortable indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To request something is to ask for it formally, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Eliminate language of fear at the outset

parts.note: Polish is the language of Poland

indicators.note: at the outset takes the opening letter of the word fear

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a language people are scared of from the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is the national language of Poland; the capital letter in the answer is hidden by the lower case 'language'.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off an opponent is to finish them, defeat them or get rid of them, so it means eliminate.

clue.text: Common sense shown by doctor with refusal to entertain books lacking in variety and interest

parts.note: MO stands for medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: to entertain is to receive a guest, so one word takes the other in

parts.note: no is a refusal
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
nous is common sense or practical intelligence

explanation.surface: A doctor's practical wisdom, plus a refusal to stock books, makes for a dull time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the long phrase at the end; 'books' is the crossword convention for the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotonous describes something tediously unvarying, the very sense of dull and lacking in variety and interest.

clue.text: Area around the mouth

indicators.note: around turns the word for region back to front

parts.note: a part is an area or region, as in 'that part of town'

explanation.surface: A simple description of the zone surrounding the lips.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single definition of a facial region; 'around' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for a person's mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: Guide and prophet residing in Troy? Just the opposite

indicators.note: residing in would put the prophet inside the other piece
just the opposite swaps the roles, so the prophet holds the other piece instead

parts.note: a seer is a prophet who foresees the future
T is an abbreviation for troy, the system of weights for precious metals

explanation.surface: A guide and a prophet, perhaps Cassandra, living in ancient Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy' suggests the city of Cassandra, but it is troy weight, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide or direct the course of something, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Daughter discovered after a short time exhausted and in a dazed state

indicators.note: discovered after says the daughter is found following the period of time

parts.note: a space can be a short period of time, as in 'in the space of a minute'
out can mean used up or exhausted, as in supplies running out

explanation.surface: A daughter turns up after a brief interval, worn out and bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced-out describes someone vague and disoriented, as if drugged or very tired, which is a dazed state.

clue.text: Playing well at centre-half in friendly

parts.note: a player who is in form is playing well

indicators.note: centre takes the middle two letters of the word half

explanation.surface: A footballer playing well at centre-half in a friendly match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre-half' is a defensive football position, but here 'centre' picks the middle letters of 'half'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means relaxed and casual, as is a friendly manner or a friendly, unofficial gathering.

clue.text: Allege as a fact following crack about German nationalist

indicators.note: following places the word for allege after the rest
about puts the word for crack around the German abbreviation

parts.note: a flaw is a crack or fault
to aver is to state firmly as true

explanation.surface: Someone asserts as fact that a crack appeared around a German nationalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag-waver is a fervent, demonstrative patriot, so the noun stands for a nationalist.

clue.text: Starts to bitch about Danish girl's insincerity

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: Faith is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone begins to complain about a Danish girl being two-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad faith is the intent to deceive, so it names dishonesty or insincerity in dealings.

clue.text: Cease to be patient after ceremony is cut short

indicators.note: after places the word for be patient behind the shortened piece
cut short removes the last letter of the word for ceremony

parts.note: form can mean ceremony or set procedure, as in 'a matter of form'
to bear something is to endure it patiently

explanation.surface: Someone stops being patient once a ceremony is curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain or hold back from doing something, a sense close to cease.

clue.text: Needed primarily for onset of rheumatism in racehorse's joint

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: Arkle was a celebrated Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s, three times winner of the Cheltenham Gold Cup

indicators.note: onset of takes the first letter of rheumatism
primarily takes the first letter of the word Needed

explanation.surface: A racehorse's joint needs attention at the first sign of rheumatism.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of 'Needed' replaces the opening letter of 'rheumatism' in ARKLE, a famous Irish racehorse, giving the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint linking foot and leg, so 'joint' defines it by example.

clue.text: Species seen around Dorset oddly having similar characteristics

indicators.note: seen around puts the word for species round the chosen letters

parts.note: a kind is a species or sort

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word Dorset

explanation.surface: A species found throughout Dorset seems to share traits.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred as an adjective means related or alike in nature, as in kindred spirits.

clue.text: Almost new organ

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A brand-new church organ that is not quite finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a musical instrument, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Near as an adverb means nearly or not far from, so it stands for almost, as in 'near perfect'.

clue.text: Succeed in obstructing sinister German socialist

indicators.note: obstructing means getting in the way, so the word sits between the other two pieces

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, a heraldic sense
to win is to succeed

explanation.surface: Success in stopping a menacing German socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' looks sinister in the menacing sense; its original Latin sense is left, used in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-winger holds radical or socialist political views, so socialist is a fair equivalent.

clue.text: That's for example up beyond Lake Superior

indicators.note: beyond means the following pieces come after the abbreviation for lake

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: eg, exempli gratia, means for example

explanation.surface: A geographical note about something lying past Lake Superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake Superior' reads as the Great Lake; Superior is the definition, in its sense of a feudal overlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord to whom service is owed, a superior in the feudal hierarchy.

clue.text: Brilliant success evident in rebuttal Cézanne sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the hidden letters are read backwards
evident in says the letters are plainly visible within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dazzling triumph shows in an answer rebutting critics of Cézanne.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'evident' in the definition; it belongs with 'in' as the signal for letters concealed in the next words, leaving 'Brilliant success' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is a dazzling triumph or notable brilliance of performance, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Hang about taking in extremely well-made still

indicators.note: taking in puts the chosen letters inside the word for linger

parts.note: to hover is to hang about or linger

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters of well-made

explanation.surface: Lingering while taking in something well-made, a moonshine still perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like a noun or adjective, but it is the adverb meaning nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: However and still both mean nevertheless, introducing a contrast, so they swap as adverbs.

clue.text: Ended with Sally stripping off altogether

parts.note: over means ended or finished

indicators.note: stripping off removes the outer letters of the name Sally

explanation.surface: It all ended with Sally taking off her clothes, appearing in the altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altogether' teases the nudity idiom 'in the altogether'; here it just means in total.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall and altogether both mean taking everything into account, in total, as adverbs.

clue.text: Painter of the Queen seen after a short walk

indicators.note: seen after says the royal abbreviation follows the stroll

parts.note: a turn is a short stroll, as in a turn around the garden
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A painter of the Queen's portrait is spotted after a brief stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. W. Turner was the great English Romantic landscape artist, so painter defines him by example.

clue.text: Questionable verdict not initially finding approval

indicators.note: questionable suggests the letters are open to doubt and may be rearranged
not initially drops the first letter of verdict

explanation.surface: A dubious verdict fails at first to win acceptance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' removes V from VERDICT, and 'Questionable' rearranges the remaining ERDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit means praise or acknowledgement given for something, as in 'credit where it is due'.
